title: BTX Electroporation User Spotlight: Insights from In Utero Electroporation
body_markdown:
A recent study, *"Mef2c Controls Postnatal Callosal Axon Targeting by Regulating Sensitivity to Ephrin Repulsion,"* explores how the transcription factor Mef2c influences callosal projection neuron (CPN) connectivity in the postnatal brain. Researchers found that Mef2c modulates the sensitivity of CPN axons to EphrinA5-mediated repulsion, ensuring proper axon navigation across the corpus callosum. Loss of Mef2c leads to misprojected axons, highlighting its crucial role in neural circuit formation.


To investigate this, the team performed in-utero electroporation with the BTX ECM 830 electroporation system to introduce genetic constructs into developing neurons, enabling precise gene manipulation. These findings have significant implications for neurodevelopmental disorders, such as autism and intellectual disability, where disrupted callosal connectivity is a hallmark feature. The study underscores the power of non-viral gene delivery for unraveling the complexities of brain development and advancing neuroscience research.


Read the full article[here](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.01.22.634300v1.full.pdf) .
